subject.title: Durable Core PR 2/6: add the opt-in shared-state foundation

question: Should OpenClaw adopt this ten-table, cross-owner durable shared-state foundation in core before the dependent gateway-recovery work is considered?
rationale: The branch is technically scoped as opt-in internal storage, but it establishes a permanent shared persistence and ownership model that VISION.md treats as exceptional core-orchestration work rather than an ordinary repair.

options.title: Sponsor the durable core boundary
options.body: Approve the owner-first residual boundary, then require a current-main rebase and explicit fresh-install/upgrade proof before merge.

options.title: Narrow to existing owners
options.body: Keep task, flow, subagent, session, and delivery evidence within their current owners and reject the new general durable tables.

options.title: Pause the stack
options.body: Leave the RFC and implementation open until a concrete user-facing recovery gap and core ownership case are accepted.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the durable core boundary
recommendation.body: Approve the owner-first residual boundary, then require a current-main rebase and explicit fresh-install/upgrade proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Repository vision and root ownership context make this a product-direction decision rather than a contributor-follow-up question.
